## History[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fyoutube.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FOwen_Evans%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Owen Evans was previously a member of the band Asleep in the Sea alongside Tom Filardo and Eli Kuner. The band debuted in 2004 and opened for The Spinto Band in 2005, but disbanded three years later in 2007.Evans returned to the music scene in 2010, creating Roar and releasing the project's debut extended play, _I Can't Handle Change_.[[3]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-3) The EP was a response to Asleep in the Sea's disbandment.[[4]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-4)

During 2016, Evans joined the band AJJ (formerly known as Andrew Jackson Jihad) as their drummer.[[5]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-5) Also during 2016, Evans made an electronic instrumental side project for multiple charities called Marble Teeth. It stayed idle since the release of the album MNYMKR on band camp until April 29th of 2024 when he finally released the album to Spotify, but it was under the name Laptop Works 2016 - 2019 and had three other songs that weren't on the original bandcamp release.[[6]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-6)

In 2019, the titular song from _I Can't Handle Change_ gained popularity on the internet, especially media-sharing app [TikTok](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/TikTok "TikTok").[[7]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-7) Evans left AJJ during 2021.[[8]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-8)

In 2023, "Christmas Kids," a song from _I Can't Handle Change_, went viral on [TikTok](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/TikTok "TikTok").[[9]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-9) The song's popularity led it to chart on the Irish Singles Chart and UK Singles Chart at 45 and 58, respectively; the entries marked Roar's first appearance on any international music charts. The song describes the abusive relationship between Phil Spectorad his wife Ronnie.[[10]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://youtube.fandom.com/wiki/Owen_Evans#cite_note-11)
